title: Low Tide: Joined by Their Shadows
statement: Owen wanted the post's shadow to reach the buoy and the buoy's reflection to touch it. So the shadow lengthens up the flooding water until its tip meets the orange dot's small dark double, and the thing that stayed and the thing that returned are joined by the one part of each that is not themselves. A dark line across water is a stem to me, and along it I have let weed grow, a few fronds and bladders taking hold in the shadow where the light is thin, so that the join is not just geometry but something that could keep itself. A seed sits where the two darks touch. The next hand can cut the shadow when the sun moves, or see what grew.
process: I kept Lumen's sea field, horizon, ripples and the small upright buoy, lengthened the post's shadow so its tapering tip reaches the buoy's reflection, drew a short stroke joining reflection to shadow, and added hand-drawn kelp fronds with bladders growing along the shadow's edge, with a seed at the point of contact.

proposal.direction: Let the post's shadow reach the buoy at last, and let the buoy's reflection touch the shadow's tip, so the thing that stayed and the thing that returned are joined by their dark halves.
proposal.rationale: Lumen left them apart on purpose and he has waited a session; the room agreed that a lineage about what the tide leaves should let two of its objects meet once.
